newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico EPR rebels appear in four towns.
newsitem.headline: Mexico EPR rebels appear in four towns.

text.p: Heavily armed Marxist rebels have appeared in four poor Mexican towns in the past three days calling for a new constitution and distributing propaganda, witnesses said on Friday.
Villagers said guerrillas from the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) entered their towns in the southwestern state of Guerrero wearing hoods and armed with AK-47 assault rifles but did not fire shots.

The EPR, which first appeared in Guerrero last June calling for the overthrow of President Ernesto Zedillo's government, has carried out attacks on police and security forces in at least five central and southern states.

EPR leaders have said in clandestine interviews with journalists that their organisation is currently in a "propaganda phase," preferring to spread its message peacefully rather than carry out armed attacks.
Police estimate the group has killed around 30 people while the guerrillas claim 96 victims.

Villagers said around 100 EPR rebels entered the remote town of San Luis San Pedro, about 70 miles (110 km) west of the Pacific Coast tourist resort of Acapulco on Tuesday night and threatened the town police commissioner. Police denied any EPR appearance.

On Wednesday night, guerrillas entered the towns of Poza Honda and Tecoanapa, on different points of the Guerrero coast. In Tecoanapa the local mayor said the rebels demanded a new constitution, then withdrew.

In the other EPR action, witnesses said the group had entered Ayahualulco, a remote village in Guerrero, on Tuesday night to hold a propaganda meeting using bullhorns. It said 10 rebels armed with AK-47 assault rifles had called on the population to join the EPR.
